name: JUNO underground experimental hall, Dashi Hill, Kaiping

coordinates.locator: Wikipedia infobox, 'Jiangmen Underground Neutrino Observatory', citing He, Miao (2014), NOW workshop presentation, p.9 (topographical map, no printed coordinate text)
coordinates.note: No rank<=7 source fetched this session states explicit numeric coordinates for the underground hall (the JUNO CDR and 'JUNO Physics and Detector' papers give only the qualitative location -- 52.5-53 km from the Yangjiang/Taishan nuclear plants, under >700 m of granite, near Kaiping/Jiangmen, Guangdong -- with no lat/lon). This value is Wikipedia's infobox coordinate, itself derived (per Wikipedia's own citation) from a 2014 conference presentation slide, not a stated numeric coordinate; per A17 it is recorded as `kind: campus`, `confidence: approximate`, not `kind: underground_lab`, and precision is set coarse (2 km) to reflect that uncertainty.

depth.quote: The experimental hall, spanning more than 50 meters, is under a granite mountain of over 700 m overburden.

notes: The underground experimental hall itself is reported as 'spanning more than 50 meters' (CDR) with a total civil-construction volume around 300,000 m^3 and a main hall of about 120,000 m^3 (per a secondary IHEP-related search summary, not independently verified against a fetched primary source in this session).

summary.plain: The rock cavern under Dashi Hill near Kaiping, in Jiangmen, southern China, where the JUNO neutrino detector sits, shielded by more than 700 metres of granite.
summary.technical: Underground experimental hall of facility:juno-jiangmen, excavated beneath Dashi Hill near Kaiping, Jiangmen, Guangdong, with over 700 m of granite overburden, 52.5-53 km from the Yangjiang and Taishan nuclear power plants.
